bbc.description: Al-Mughayyir's council says they were trying to stop settlers stealing sheep, but the Israeli military says they threw stones at its troops.

bbc.description: Jeffery was known for playing cheerleader Bree in 2018 Disney Channel movie Zombies and two sequels.

bbc.description: The ICE officer faces federal charges related to the January shooting in Minnesota.

bbc.description: Rescuers found 44 survivors on board the vessel but bad weather meant they had to leave five bodies behind.

bbc.description: Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode is charged in Nigeria with offences including causing death by dangerous driving.

rfi.title: Culture or Kremlin influence? Europe divided over its Russian Houses
rfi.description: A dispute between Germany and Russia over their cultural centres is drawing fresh attention to a network of Russian Houses that has faced years of accusations of propaganda and espionage, but continues to operate in several European countries.

rfi.title: British, French leaders hold talks on migrants and EU relations
rfi.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron held their first official talks on Thursday, with migrant boats, Ukraine and British-EU relations high on the agenda.

rfi.title: Former RFI journalist disappears in Niger after attempted coup
rfi.description: Reporters Without Borders has called for an investigation into the disappearance of Moussa Kaka, the director of a television station in Niger and a former correspondent for Radio France International, days after a failed coup in the country.

rfi.title: France asserts sovereignty over disputed Pacific islands as Vanuatu turns to ICJ
rfi.description: France has insisted on its sovereignty over two Pacific islands claimed by Vanuatu, which has opened a case at the International Court of Justice.

rfi.title: EU lawmakers demand Brussels force Meta to 'protect' European children
rfi.description: European Union lawmakers have demanded that the bloc's executive compel Meta to change the "addictive" design of its platforms in Europe, as the giant has promised to do in some US states, according to a letter seen by the French news agency AFP on Thursday.

rfi.title: Three Pacific hurricanes gather strength as El Nino intensifies
rfi.description: The current El Nino could become the strongest on record as the natural climate pattern that warms the tropical Pacific intensifies, with three hurricanes churning across the ocean on Thursday. The United Nations has warned of growing extreme weather risks into 2027.

rfi.title: Ebola deaths in DR Congo top 3,000 as WHO says vaccine trials imminent
rfi.description: More than 3,000 people have died of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the latest figures show, as the World Health Organisation says trials of three potential vaccines against the strain behind the current outbreak should begin within weeks.

rfi.title: Nepal seeks climate justice after Himalayan disaster
rfi.description: When a wall of icy debris from a glacial collapse on the China-Nepal border tore through his village last week, Pemba Chhring Tamang watched the landscape he had known all his life disappear.

rfi.title: EU suspends Brazilian meat imports over antibiotic concerns
rfi.description: The European Union has suspended imports of Brazilian meat and other animal products, as Brussels waits for assurances that the South American country is complying with the bloc’s rules on antibiotic use in livestock farming.

rfi.title: French filmmakers and local fixer freed after weeks in Togo detention
rfi.description: Two French documentary makers and their Togolese fixer have been granted provisional release in Togo, more than a month after they were arrested in the north while working on a television programme. The three deny accusations of false statements and irregularities linked to their filming assignment.

rfi.title: EU summons Russian envoy, eyes sanctions after Germany drone 'attack'
rfi.description: The European Union summoned Russia's top diplomat and signaled it may impose new sanctions on Wednesday, after last month's drone incident in Germany that the bloc's foreign policy chief branded "state-sponsored terrorism."

rfi.title: World set to breach 1.5C climate limit as UN urges rapid reversal
rfi.description: Global warming is set to cross the 1.5C limit within the next few years, exposing people and ecosystems to more severe climate damage, the UN's environmental agency said on Wednesday. But temperatures could eventually be brought back down if emissions fall sharply and carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere.

rfi.title: Senegal and IMF strike $2.2bn deal, two years after debt scandal froze funding
rfi.description: Senegal and the International Monetary Fund have reached a staff-level agreement on a new $2.2 billion (€1.9 billion) lending programme, nearly two years after an earlier deal was suspended following the discovery of previously unreported public debt.

rfi.title: French pop star Patrick Bruel cancels 35-date tour amid sexual assault storm
rfi.description: French pop and variety singer Patrick Bruel has cancelled his entire 35-date autumn tour, bowing to weeks of pressure from politicians, mayors and feminist groups following allegations of sexual assault and rape against him. Lawyers representing the accusers called the decision a "power signal" showing that women are "at last being heard."

rfi.title: Tunisia accused of shutting down civil society through sweeping crackdown
rfi.description: Tunisian authorities have intensified pressure on civil society through arrests, prosecutions, financial investigations and mass suspensions, Human Rights Watch said on Wednesday – warning that the independent civic space created after the 2011 revolution has been all but shut down.

rfi.title: Clooney kicks off Venice as festival wades into war, Gaza and AI
rfi.description: Venice rolls out the red carpet Wednesday, with George Clooney set to collect a lifetime achievement award as the film festival opens a starry two-week run heavy on biopics, war-zone dramas from Gaza and Iran, and a fresh reckoning with artificial intelligence.

rfi.title: Nepal glacier disaster toll passes 1,000 as calls for climate justice grow
rfi.description: The death toll from last week's devastating Himalayan glacial floods passed 1,000 on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors. Nepal's foreign minister said the disaster was "a warning signal" of the growing risks posed by climate change.

rfi.title: DRC school year begins amid Ebola, strikes and conflict
rfi.description: Millions of students returned to school across the Democratic Republic of Congo on Tuesday, but the new term began amid an Ebola outbreak affecting six provinces, a teachers’ strike call and continuing conflict in the east. In AFC/M23-controlled territories, the movement organised the return to classrooms even as Kinshasa continued to pay primary and secondary school teachers.

euronews.title: AI is starting to see migraine as more than just a headache
euronews.description: Researchers used artificial intelligence and genetic data from more than 43,000 people to identify biological patterns that could reshape how one of the world’s most common neurological disorders is diagnosed and treated.

euronews.title: Trump administration pushes to remove tax exemptions for private universities with DEI policies
euronews.description: The Trump administration says its proposed legislation aims to make university equal and accessible to all and end “woke” campaigns which deliberately favour certain students over others due to socioeconomic or racial backgrounds.

euronews.title: Iran hits US military targets in the region as Washington probes deadly wedding strike
euronews.description: Oil prices again spiked this week after a few weeks of relative stability following the renewed fighting as Iran continues to maintain a stranglehold over the strategic Strait of Hormuz, responsible for roughly 20% of global oil shipping.

euronews.title: Berlin airport terminal evacuated after hazardous materials alert
euronews.description: A woman reports carrying toxic substances in her handbag at Berlin airport. Police arrest her and evacuate Terminal 1.

euronews.title: Trump hints US may not back UK over Falkland Islands, citing lack of Iran support
euronews.description: The US recognises Britain's administration of the Falkland Islands but remains neutral over the competing sovereignty claims.

euronews.title: 'Highly likely' Russia will escalate attacks on EU, Lithuanian minister says
euronews.description: While commending Berlin for attributing the attempted Leipzig drone attack to Russia, Lithuania's foreign affairs minister warns stronger EU-wide deterrence is needed to prevent further escalation.

euronews.title: France had its hottest summer since records began over a century ago, environment minister says
euronews.description: According to Meteo France, the summer of 2026 recorded an average temperature of 24 °C covering day and nighttime, 3.6 C above the normal average, and higher than in 2003, when temperatures were 2.7 C above normal.

euronews.title: Lisbon: MOTELX launches 20th edition with expanded programme and plenty of horror
euronews.description: Marking its 20th edition, the festival stretches over more days and more venues, packed with new discoveries and cult favourites at Portugal's scariest film event.

euronews.title: Former French President Hollande publishes new book with plan for France, but remains undecided about running
euronews.description: Former French President Hollande published his newest book on Thursday, laying out 80 policy proposals. Despite his book somewhat resembling a manifesto, the former president maintains he will wait until December to decide whether to run.

euronews.title: 'Anti-fast-fashion' law: France rejects China's discrimination claims
euronews.description: China has claimed that the new "anti-fast-fashion" law which came into force in France on Tuesday amounts to "discrimination." Responding to these accusations, a source from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs told Euronews that such claims were false.

euronews.title: Two arrested after attack on defence companies in Munich
euronews.description: In Munich, a man and a woman allegedly attempted to carry out an arson attack outside the premises of two defence companies. The pair were arrested.

euronews.title: Russians skewer authorities for ordering citizens to register their chicken
euronews.description: A government decree requiring registration of domestic birds, camels and reindeer took effect Tuesday, sending Russians to government service centres with live chickens in tow before authorities clarified that owners did not need to bring their animals anywhere.

euronews.title: Iranian café chain mogul jailed and stripped of assets for backing January protests
euronews.description: Sadegh Saeedinia, manager of the Saeedinia café chain, was convicted of "propaganda against national security" for posting about the January protests on Instagram and encouraging staff to strike, in one of the harshest sentences handed to a private entrepreneur since the unrest.

euronews.title: France tests Tesla self-driving two months after calling it too risky
euronews.description: After a "constructive exchange" on Wednesday evening between Elon Musk and Philippe Tabarot, the transport minister hailed "a new step" in authorising this type of vehicle.

euronews.title: Thousands of Ukrainian children still at risk in Russia as EU prepares new sanctions
euronews.description: Thousands of Ukrainian children remain under Russian control, facing indoctrination, militarisation and the loss of their identity, the Bring Kids Back UA initiative warned as the EU prepares new sanctions against those responsible for their deportation.

euronews.title: How public-private partnerships are driving new investment
euronews.description: Public-private partnerships are opening new opportunities for investment and development, from renewable energy and digital infrastructure to water and desalination. The episode looks at how cooperation between government and business could shape Azerbaijan’s next phase of growth.

euronews.title: EU suspension of Brazilian meat comes into force, despite ongoing talks with Brasília
euronews.description: Brazil has yet to provide the necessary guarantees to allow an audit of its beef exports’ compliance with EU food safety standards, while inspections of poultry and honey imports are already under way.

euronews.title: Macron and Burnham hail stronger UK-France ties at Downing Street talks
euronews.description: Burnham and his wife, Marie-France van Heel, welcomed the French president and First Lady Brigitte Macron outside the famous black door of 10 Downing Street.

lemonde.title: A Kiev, une fusillade entre membres des services de renseignement met en lumière les rivalités qui traversent l’appareil sécuritaire ukrainien
lemonde.description: Un affrontement armé entre agents du service de sécurité d’Ukraine et une unité spéciale du renseignement militaire a éclaté, mercredi 2 septembre, en plein centre de la capitale, forçant Volodymyr Zelensky à ordonner l’ouverture d’une enquête.

lemonde.title: Rénovation thermique des écoles : le gouvernement ampute le plan d’urgence canicule de 40 millions d’euros
lemonde.description: Fin juin, en pleine canicule, une enveloppe de près de 60 millions d’euros avait été annoncée par la Banque des territoires et le programme Actee, qui finance la rénovation thermique des bâtiments publics des collectivités locales, afin d’équiper des établissements scolaires d’ici à l’été 2027.

lemonde.title: Radio France : pour Sibyle Veil, « c’est la grandeur du service public que d’être pluraliste »
lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », la présidente-directrice générale de Radio France confirme, malgré la menace de grève, maintenir le recrutement d’un journaliste de « Valeurs actuelles » à l’éditorial politique du dimanche sur France Inter. Elle répond aussi, pour la première fois, à Thomas Legrand qui l’accuse d’avoir cédé aux pressions de l’extrême droite.

lemonde.title: De l’école au lycée, l’apprentissage au défi de l’IA : « Une réponse immédiate comble le désir de savoir, mais tue le désir d’apprendre »
lemonde.description: Si l’intelligence artificielle générative est entrée dans la vie des élèves, difficile de savoir quelles transformations elle produira dans leur manière de mémoriser et de raisonner.

lemonde.title: Après les inondations dans l’Himalaya, la Chine impose un contrôle strict des informations liées au Tibet
lemonde.description: Depuis la catastrophe du 26 août, la couverture de l’actualité de la région, hautement sensible pour les autorités, est réduite aux informations données par Pékin, qui fait la part belle aux opérations de secours. Le pouvoir censure les contenus publiés par les citoyens et bannit l’accès à la zone meurtrie pour les journalistes étrangers.

lemonde.title: Handicap : délais, droits, montant d’aides… pourquoi autant d’inégalités entre les territoires ?
lemonde.description: Alors que la Conférence nationale du handicap se réunit vendredi 4 septembre pour définir les grands chantiers du secteur, les personnes en situation de handicap continuent à subir des disparités de traitement selon le département où elles vivent.

lemonde.title: Gaël Monfils a offert son dernier spectacle en Grand Chelem, éliminé au deuxième tour de l’US Open
lemonde.description: Le joueur français de 40 ans n’a rien pu faire face à son cadet de vingt ans, l’Américain Learner Tien, 15e mondial, vainqueur en trois sets. Avant de prendre sa retraite à la fin de la saison, « La Monf » a reçu un dernier hommage du public new-yorkais.

lemonde.title: Lille passe en tête de la Ligue 1 en s’imposant difficilement à Toulouse
lemonde.description: Longtemps bousculés, les Nordistes ont fait preuve de réalisme en marquant le seul but du match à la 73e minute, grâce à Ayase Ueda, en ouverture de la troisième journée du championnat de France de football. La recrue japonaise est arrivée lundi en provenance du club néerlandais de Feyenoord.

lemonde.title: A Lyon, agressions racistes et affrontements entre supporteurs rivaux autour du stade de l’OL
lemonde.description: Une élue agressée, son compagnon blessé, un adolescent hospitalisé. La violence à connotation raciste marque le début de saison du club lyonnais. Les autorités évoquent des affrontements entre supporteurs, qui pourraient être le point de départ de ce climat de violence.

lemonde.title: Singapour, un rêve qui ne tient pas ses promesses pour les travailleurs migrants
lemonde.description: Majoritairement originaires d’Inde ou du Bangladesh, ils s’endettent lourdement pour venir dans l’espoir de faire vivre leur famille, avant de déchanter face aux salaires et aux conditions de travail très éloignés de ce qui leur avait été promis.

lemonde.title: A deux mois des élections de mi-mandat, l’administration Trump repart à l’offensive sur le vote par correspondance
lemonde.description: L’exécutif américain a de nouveau demandé à la Cour suprême, jeudi, de lui permettre d’appliquer un décret visant à encadrer plus strictement le vote par correspondance, une mesure contestée en justice par plusieurs Etats gouvernés par des démocrates.

lemonde.title: La FIFA dénonce une « campagne de dénigrement » menée par l’UEFA à son égard
lemonde.description: Dans le sillage du projet économique avorté de la FIFA, l’instance européenne prépare une action en justice contre le patron du football mondial, Gianni Infantino, pour « gestion déloyale ».

lemonde.title: Volkswagen s’accorde sur une restructuration historique, 100 000 emplois supprimés en perspective d’ici à 2030
lemonde.description: Le constructeur allemand estime qu’une « adaptation conséquente des capacités de personnel à la réalité économique est indispensable », en raison de la pression concurrentielle mondiale croissante, des mutations de la demande et de la technologie.

lemonde.title: OpenAI lance GPT-6, son premier modèle d’IA capable de pirater seul des systèmes informatiques très protégés
lemonde.description: Classé par l’entreprise au niveau de risque maximal en matière de cybersécurité, GPT-6 Astra sera disponible « dans les prochains jours » pour les abonnés payants de ChatGPT, l’agent conversationnel utilisé par un milliard de personnes chaque semaine, selon OpenAI.

lemonde.title: Au procès de Bertrand Venteau, le président de la Coordination rurale, deux mondes qui s’opposent
lemonde.description: Devant le tribunal correctionnel d’Auch, jeudi 3 septembre, le syndicaliste agricole a reconnu et assumé les propos qu’il avait tenus le 19 décembre 2025, quand il disait vouloir « faire la peau aux écolos ».

lemonde.title: Au Brésil, la Cour suprême ébranlée par des soupçons de corruption, Lula exige une enquête impartiale
lemonde.description: La crise a éclaté après la publication d’un rapport de police faisant état d’échanges entre le banquier Daniel Vorcaro, incarcéré pour malversations, et le juge Alexandre de Moraes, dont le rôle avait été central dans la condamnation de Jair Bolsonaro pour tentative de coup d’Etat, en 2025.

france24fr.title: Revendication de l'Argentine sur les Malouines : dopé par Donald Trump, Javier Milei durcit le ton
france24fr.description: Le président argentin Javier Milei a annoncé jeudi un projet de loi renforçant les sanctions contre toute activité non autorisée autour des Malouines, l'archipel de l'Atlantique Sud, dont Buenos Aires et Londres se disputent la souveraineté. Plus tôt cette semaine, Donald Trump n'a pas exclu de revoir la neutralité américaine sur la souveraineté des îles.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient en direct : la Corée du Sud envisage de contribuer à sécuriser le détroit d'Ormuz
france24fr.description: La Corée du Sud envisage d'apporter sa "contribution" pour sécuriser la navigation dans le détroit stratégique d'Ormuz, verrouillé depuis le début de la guerre entre les États-Unis et l'Iran, a indiqué vendredi la présidence du pays. L'Iran a de nouveau visé jeudi des cibles militaires américaines dans le Golfe, jurant de venger l'attaque qui a tué quatre personnes lors d'un mariage mardi soir, frappe pour laquelle Washington a annoncé une enquête. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: OpenAI lance GPT-6 Astra, son premier modèle capable de pirater seul des systèmes protégés
france24fr.description: Classé au plus haut niveau de risque en cybersécurité par OpenAI lui-même, le modèle d'intelligence artificielle GPT-6 Astra, lancé jeudi, est capable de pirater seul des systèmes informatiques très protégés. Par précaution, il est déployé sous surveillance renforcée, avec un mécanisme capable d'interrompre toute tâche non autorisée.

france24fr.title: En Italie, Giorgia Meloni bat un record de longévité et lance sa campagne pour 2027
france24fr.description: La présidente du Conseil italienne Giorgia Meloni franchit vendredi le cap des 1 413 jours à la tête du gouvernement, devançant Silvio Berlusconi. Un record de longévité considéré par son camp comme un atout de campagne pour les législatives de 2027, alors que certains experts pointent le manque de résultats concrets sur la croissance et le pouvoir d'achat.

france24fr.title: Restructuration historique chez Volkswagen : 100 000 suppressions de postes d'ici 2030
france24fr.description: Le conseil de surveillance du constructeur allemand Volkswagen a approuvé jeudi à l'unanimité un plan de restructuration inédit, ajoutant 50 000 suppressions d'emploi aux 50 000 déjà actées en Allemagne depuis 2024. Au total, environ 15 % des effectifs mondiaux du groupe sont concernés.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : la Cour de cassation confirme les lourdes peines dans l’affaire du "complot contre l’État"
france24fr.description: La Cour de cassation tunisienne a rejeté jeudi le pourvoi dans l’affaire du "complot contre la sûreté de l’État", confirmant les lourdes peines prononcées en appel, en novembre 2025, contre une quarantaine de personnes, dont des figures de l’opposition et des avocats.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : la Cour de cassation confirme les lourdes peines dans l’affaire du "complot contre l’État"
france24fr.description: La Cour de cassation tunisienne a rejeté jeudi le pourvoi dans l’affaire du "complot contre la sûreté de l’État", confirmant les lourdes peines prononcées en appel, en novembre 2025, contre une quarantaine de personnes, dont des figures de l’opposition et des avocats.

france24fr.title: Iran : les Etats-Unis ont-ils visé une cérémonie de mariage ?
france24fr.description: Dans leurs frappes récentes contre l'Iran, les Etats-Unis sont accusés d'avoir bombardé une cérémonie de mariage, dans la région du détroit d'Ormuz. Des images vérifiées tournées après l'attaque montrent les dégâts qu'elle a occasionnés et les décombres alentour. L'armée américaine a assuré ne pas viser de civils.

france24fr.title: Ambassade de France en Irak : les descendants de propriétaires juifs assignent l’État français
france24fr.description: Nouveau front judiciaire dans le litige autour de l’ambassade de France en Irak. Les descendants des propriétaires juifs du bâtiment ont assigné l’État français à Paris et réclament 21,5 millions d’euros, une somme correspondant selon eux aux loyers impayés depuis plus de cinquante ans et au préjudice moral subi.

france24fr.title: L'extrême droite en tête des élections régionales en Allemagne : le retour des vieux démons ?
france24fr.description: L’AfD, le parti d’extrême droite en Allemagne, est bien placé pour remporter la victoire dans le Land de Saxe-Anhalt dans l'Est du pays dimanche 6 septembre. Cela serait la première fois qu’un parti d’extrême droite prendrait le pouvoir depuis 1945. L’AfD est en tête dans les sondages avec près de 40% des intentions de vote. Sa tête de liste Ulrich Siegmund est une star des réseaux sociaux. En quoi ce scrutin régional est-il décisif pour l’Allemagne et pour l’Europe ? Quelle est la ligne de ce p

france24fr.title: Football : s'estimant "humilié" Aubameyang ne veut plus jouer avec le Gabon
france24fr.description: ⚽🇬🇦 Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang ne veut plus jouer avec le Gabon. Le capitaine des Panthères a annoncé sa mise en retrait de l’équipe nationale, s’estimant "humilié" après son exclusion puis sa réintégration à la suite de l’échec à la CAN 2025 au Maroc.

france24fr.title: "On n’aura plus d’automne ni d’hiver" : pourquoi l’épisode El Niño attendu fin 2026 inquiète
france24fr.description: L’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM) a annoncé jeudi que le phénomène climatique El Niño va se renforcer dans les prochains mois pour atteindre une intensité "très forte" d’ici la fin de l’année et se maintenir jusqu'en février 2027. Sécheresses, inondations, chaleurs extrêmes : décryptage d’un phénomène naturel dont les effets sont amplifiés par le réchauffement climatique.

france24fr.title: À Kiev, l’étrange guerre des espions ukrainiens en plein conflit avec la Russie
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky a rappelé à l’ordre, mercredi, les deux principaux services de renseignement du pays dont les membres se sont tirés dessus. Un incident qui révèle la rivalité entre les espions ukrainiens.

france24fr.title: Italie : le combat d'une famille pour scolariser leur enfant
france24fr.description: Au large de la Sicile, sur l'île de Stromboli, le plus petite école d'Europe rouvre ses portes pour une seule élève, Aïsha.

france24fr.title: Agriculture : une serre adaptée aux futures canicules
france24fr.description: Le changement climatique pousse à adapter les manières de cultiver. Ces serres spéciales pourrait être une partie de la solution. Elle permettent de continuer à faire pousser fruits et légumes malgré des épisodes caniculaires intenses

france24fr.title: Pourquoi ces jeunes des quartiers partent gravir un sommet dans les Alpes ?
france24fr.description: Et si la montagne pouvait rapprocher les jeunes des quartiers populaires de ceux qui n’y vivent pas ? À Nantes, quatre jeunes se lancent dans une aventure hors du commun : une semaine d’alpinisme dans les Alpes, accompagnés de mentors issus du monde professionnel.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : une nouvelle étape franchie dans la lutte contre la drépanocytose
france24fr.description: Au Sénégal, un médicament générique fabriqué sur place redonne espoir aux malades de drépanocytose. Une avancée qui permet de réduire la dépendance du continent vis à vis des médicaments importés d'Europe et des États-Unis.

france24fr.title: Iran : "leur monnaie ne vaut plus rien" se félicite Donald Trump
france24fr.description: Suite aux frappes américaines menées contre l'Iran, le pays est en pleine récession économique. Les commerçants n'ont parfois pas d'autre choix que de fermer leur magasin alors que les autorités iraniennes tentent de maintenir, comme elles le peuvent, l'économie du pays.

Giorgia Meloni: Machtmaschine Meloni – wie die Postfaschistin Italien verändert hat
zeit.description: Am 4. September stellt Giorgia Meloni einen Rekord auf: 1.413 Tage im Amt. Länger als jeder Regierungschef der Republik. War die Angst vor der Postfaschistin übertrieben?

zeit.title: Literaturfestival: Kermani, Emcke und Regener bei Lit.Cologne Spezial
Volkswagen in Wolfsburg: Wende in Wolfsburg
zeit.description: Überraschend hat sich der VW-Aufsichtsrat auf ein umfassendes Sparprogramm geeinigt. Was hat das für Folgen? Und: Warum Giorgia Meloni in Italien so stark bleibt.

zeit.title: Elbvertiefung: Der tägliche Newsletter aus Hamburg: Die geheimnisvolle Frikadelle
zeit.description: Die Elbvertiefung am Freitag – Mit einem Hamburger Opa gegen rechts, einem 18-Jährigen, der »White Tiger« nacheiferte, und einem Festival gegen das Clubsterben.

zeit.title: Berühmte Kunst: Farbenprächtige Tierwelten – Franz Marc in Düsseldorf
Wiedervereinigung: Ist die deutsche Einheit gelungen, Steffen Mau?
zeit.description: Der Soziologe Steffen Mau erklärt, was man bei der Wiedervereinigung hätte besser machen können und warum der Osten politisch so anders tickt.

zeit.title: Reinhold Heil: »Ich mache mein Lieblingsmüsli seit 1984«
zeit.description: Im Wochenendpodcast erzählt der Musiker Reinhold Heil die wahre Geschichte seines Songs »Carbonara«. Und verrät ein Müsli-Rezept, das sich bewährt hat.

zeit.title: Reaktionen auf VW-Sanierung: Olaf Lies sieht in VW-Sparplan »zukunftsfähiges Konzept«
zeit.description: Der Autokonzern stehe vor enormen Herausforderungen, sagt der niedersächsische Ministerpräsident. VW-Betriebsrat und IG Metall zeigen sich erst mal zufrieden.

zeit.title: Irankrieg: Vance will Irankrieg nicht als Krieg bezeichnen
zeit.description: Laut US-Vizepräsident JD Vance haben die USA ihre Einsätze im Iran beendet. Verhandeln will das Land erst, wenn der Iran Angriffe auf Schiffe einstellt. Das Liveblog

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Im Nahen Osten entsteht eine neue Ordnung. Friedlicher wird die Region deshalb aber nicht
nzz.description: Der Mekka-Pakt zwischen Saudiarabien, der Türkei und Pakistan zeigt: Im Nahen Osten übernehmen jetzt die Sunniten die Macht. Mehr Sicherheit entsteht dadurch aber nicht. Dafür brauchen die Araber einen Mentalitätswandel.

nzz.title: 70 000 flohen nach Ceuta – und noch viel mehr wollen Marokko verlassen. Dabei boomt das Land. Was ist da los?
nzz.description: Reise durch ein Land, das seine Jungen verliert.

nzz.title: NBA-Strafen: Eine Schmach für den Microsoft-Milliardär Steve Ballmer, ein Triumph für den Journalismus – und Erinnerungen an den HC Lugano
nzz.description: Die NBA verhängt drakonische Strafen gegen die Los Angeles Clippers, die versucht hatten, das System auszudribbeln. Der Mecano erinnert an jenen des HC Lugano rund um die Jahrtausendwende.

nzz.title: «Was für ein König!»: Wie Norwegens Schriftsteller um Harald V. trauern
nzz.description: Hinter der grossen Trauer um den Monarchen werden auch die ungelösten Konflikte im Königshaus sichtbar.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Mehr Unternehmer, weniger Staatsbauern: Die Agrarreform von Guy Parmelin bleibt auf halber Strecke stehen
nzz.description: Der Bundesrat fordert von den Landwirten mehr «KMU-Spirit». Doch wer die Bauern zu Unternehmern machen will, muss ihnen auch mehr Markt und Wettbewerb zumuten.

nzz.title: Deutschland lebt nicht mehr im sicheren Hinterland
nzz.description: Russland trägt seinen Krieg zunehmend über die Ukraine hinaus. Der Anschlagsversuch von Leipzig zwingt die deutsche Regierung zu einer unbequemen Erkenntnis: Wer Putin abschrecken will, kann nicht jedes Risiko einer russischen Reaktion vermeiden.

nzz.title: Der Täter von Aarau nutzte eine Kalaschnikow, die er heute wohl nicht mehr erwerben dürfte: Muss das Waffenrecht trotzdem angepasst werden?
nzz.description: Den Waffenschein erhielt der heute 43-Jährige vor mehr als zwanzig Jahren – und das unter anderem für ein Gewehr, das heute so gut wie verboten ist. Das wirft Fragen auf und führt zu Forderungen in der Politik.

nzz.title: Als Antwort auf den Hitzesommer: Die «Kartoffelfans» fordern einen neuen Umgang mit Gentechnik
nzz.description: Wolle man in Zukunft genug Kartoffeln in der Schweiz haben, so sagen die Branchenvertreter in der Zürcher Wasserkirche, brauche es eine Teilliberalisierung von neuen Zuchtmethoden.

nzz.title: Die Niederlande ziehen 78 Tonnen Gold aus New York ab – warum Notenbanken Trumps Amerika zunehmend misstrauen
nzz.description: Weltweit machen sich Notenbanken unabhängiger von den USA und dem Dollar. Für die Schweiz präsentiert sich die Ausgangslage anders.

nzz.title: Wegen Kritik am Krieg: Russlands Mutter Teresa drohen bis zu zehn Jahre Haft
nzz.description: Lida Moniawa widmet sich seit ihrer Jugend den Schwächsten der russischen Gesellschaft. Nach Russlands Überfall auf die Ukraine blieb sie bewusst in Moskau, kritisierte den Krieg. Nun will der Staat sie zum Schweigen bringen. Im Regime Putin ist niemand sicher.

nzz.title: Drohnen gegen Haie: Australien will seine Strände besser sichern
nzz.description: Nach mehreren tödlichen Angriffen durch Haie sichert Sydney die Strände aus der Luft und mit neuen Sensoren. Experten warnen aber vor falscher Sicherheit.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Je weniger der Körper bei der Arbeit zählt, desto mehr wird er zum Statussymbol», sagt der Sportsoziologe
nzz.description: Seit einem Vierteljahrhundert erforscht Markus Lamprecht, wie die Schweiz Sport treibt. Er erklärt, warum ihn das Wort «Vereinssterben» nervt – und weshalb Pumpen das neue Turnen ist.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Fahrrad oder schnelles E-Bike: Ab wann rechnet sich der Umstieg?
nzz.description: Ein Fahrrad ohne E-Antrieb kostet pro Kilometer deutlich weniger als ein schnelles E-Bike. Entscheidend bei der Wahl des Zweirads für den Arbeitsweg sind Distanz, Höhenmeter und Fahrleistung.

nzz.title: Der Verein, der die Neutralitätsdebatte beeinflusste und der Ukraine Waffen liefern will
nzz.description: Ein Verein trug mit einer Umfrage massgeblich dazu bei, dass das Parlament auf einen Gegenvorschlag zur Neutralitätsinitiative verzichtete. Mit dem absehbaren Volks-Nein will er sich nicht zufriedengeben.

nzz.title: «Positive Energie» statt schreckliche Bilder – wie Chinas Regierung den Diskurs zur Sturzflut an der Grenze zu Nepal lenkt
nzz.description: Peking will verhindern, dass die Frage nach der Verantwortung für die Katastrophe aufkommt. Deshalb hält die Regierung kritische Berichterstatter fern – und feiert die Helfer als Helden.

nzz.title: Das «leuchtende Vorbild» der AfD: Die FPÖ ist in Österreich seit Jahren Teil der Machtelite – mit wenig Erfolg
nzz.description: Die deutsche Rechtspartei will von der Schwesterpartei im Nachbarland lernen, wie Regieren geht. Allerdings endeten Koalitionen mit der FPÖ auf Bundesebene stets vorzeitig und im Chaos.

spiegel.title: Restaurants, Schwimmbäder, Museen, überall muss man heute Slots buchen. Ist das noch echte Freizeit?
Sachsen-Anhalt: Wie die AfD auch ohne Mehrheit an die Macht käme
spiegel.description: Die Rechtsextremen werden die Wahl in Sachsen-Anhalt wohl klar gewinnen – aber wenige Stimmen könnten entscheiden, wer am Ende regiert. Fünf Szenarien für den Wahlausgang.

spiegel.title: News: Wahl in Sachsen-Anhalt, AfD, Ceuta, Annalena Baerbock
spiegel.description: Die AfD unterscheidet sich von anderen rechten Parteien in Europa. In Ceuta nehmen Übegriffe gegen Migrantinnen und Migranten zu. Und: Annalena Baerbocks Amtszeit bei der Uno endet. Das ist die Lage am Freitagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Der Gastro-Code: 18 Fragen rund ums Essengehen – und Antworten von Profis
spiegel.description: Wie man ein Gericht von der Karte bestellt, obwohl man den Namen nicht aussprechen kann. Warum es ein No-Go ist, die Jacke mit an den Platz zu nehmen. 18 Fragen rund ums Essengehen – und Antworten von Profis.

spiegel.title: Wegovy & Mounjaro: So essen Sie richtig, um beim Abnehmen Ihre Muskeln zu erhalten
spiegel.description: Wer Abnehmmedikamente nimmt, möchte Fett abbauen – sollte Muskelmasse aber bewahren. Was also essen? Experten erklären, worauf man achten sollte.

spiegel.title: Tennis: Nick Kyrgios nach Kokain-Sperre bereits wieder startberechtigt
spiegel.description: Tennis-Badboy Nick Kyrgios hatte sich auf Mallorca mit Kokain im Blut erwischen lassen. Jetzt steht das Strafmaß des Verbandes fest. Kurios daran: Der Australier kann sofort wieder bei Turnieren antreten.

spiegel.title: Experten machen US-Munition für Tote auf Hochzeit in Iran verantwortlich
spiegel.description: Vier Menschen starben nach einer Explosion auf einer Hochzeit in Iran, Dutzende wurden verletzt. Waffenexperte haben nun Fotos vom Unglücksort analysiert und kommen zu einem klaren Urteil.

spiegel.title: Dormagen: Polizei geht von versuchter Sabotage an Umspannwerk aus
spiegel.description: Ein Spaziergänger hatte einen verdächtigen Gegenstand entdeckt. Jetzt erklären die Ermittler: Im neuen Fall in Dormagen dürfte es sich um versuchte Sabotage handeln. Ein Bekennerschreiben liegt demnach vor.

spiegel.title: Niederlage für Donald Trump – Gericht in Missouri kippt Neuzuschnitt der Wahlkreise
spiegel.description: Mit dem Verschieben von Wahlkreisgrenzen wollen Donald Trumps Republikaner ihre Chancen bei den Zwischenwahlen in diversen Bundesstaaten verbessern. In Missouri hat ein Gericht die umstrittene Praxis nun gestoppt.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Präsident will Supreme-Court-Entscheid zu schärferen Briefwahlregeln
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident verbreitet mit schöner Regelmäßigkeit das Märchen vom Betrug per Briefwahl. Nun will er die Post zwingen, schärfere Regeln anzuwenden. Die Erlaubnis soll vom Supreme Court kommen, im Blitzverfahren.

spiegel.title: Gianni Infantino: Fifa wirft Uefa »Verleumdungskampagne« vor
spiegel.description: Gianni Infantino hat sich mit seinen Investorenplänen verzockt. Europas Fußballverband Uefa will juristisch gegen den wankenden Fifa-Präsidenten vorgehen. Nun startet der Weltverband einen Gegenangriff auf die Europäer.

spiegel.title: Krieg in der Ukraine: US-Vermittler reisen offenbar nach Moskau und Kyjiw
spiegel.description: Seit Monaten wartet der ukrainische Präsident auf einen Besuch von US-Gesandten in seinem Land. Nun sollen laut Wolodymyr Selenskyj Friedensgespräche sowohl in Moskau als auch in Kyjiw stattfinden.

spiegel.title: Volkswagen in der Krise: Aufsichtsrat stimmt Sanierungsplan zu
spiegel.description: Weitere 50.000 Jobs sollen wegfallen, vier Werke stehen auf der Kippe: Der Aufsichtsrat hat den VW-​Sanierungsplan gebilligt.

spiegel.title: Spahn wird Mitglied des Haushaltsausschusses
spiegel.description: Die politische Karriere von Jens Spahn geht weiter. Erst Mitte Juli war er nach scharfer Kritik als Fraktionschef der Union zurückgetreten. Nun zieht er in einen der einflussreichsten Ausschüsse des Bundestages ein.

spiegel.title: Hape Kerkeling warnt vor »Kapitulation der Fakten vor der Lautstärke«
spiegel.description: Entertainer Hape Kerkeling hat die SPD-Abgeordneten an den Mut ihres ehemaligen Parteivorsitzenden Otto Wels erinnert. Und sie aufgefordert: Das Land dürfe Verfassungsfeinden und deren Gegnern nicht denselben Raum lassen.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt - News zur Landtagswahl: Didi Hallervorden nennt Schulze den »richtigen Mann« für Sachsen-Anhalt
spiegel.description: Kabarettist Dieter Hallervorden ruft in Halle dazu auf, gegen die AfD zu stimmen. Den Kanzler kritisiert er trotzdem. Und: Ein Viertel der Wähler ist laut ZDF-Politbarometer kurz vor dem Urnengang noch unentschlossen. Das News-Update.

spiegel.title: CDU in Sachsen-Anhalt: Drei Tage vor der Wahl eskaliert der Streit
spiegel.description: Die CDU in Sachsen-Anhalt taumelt der Wahl entgegen. Der Kanzler wird im Wahlkampf versteckt. Die Umfragen sind schlecht. Jetzt kommt noch ein offener Zwist über den Umgang mit der Linken dazu.

spiegel.title: Brandenburg: Polizei prüft Bekennerschreiben zu Angriff auf Stromnetz
spiegel.description: Zu dem Angriff auf die Stromversorgungsanlage in Jänschwalde ist ein Bekennerschreiben aufgetaucht. Die Polizei prüft auch Hinweise aus der Bevölkerung. Brandenburg will rasch Konsequenzen ziehen.

observador.title: Os segredos do recorde surpresa de Giorgia Meloni
observador.description: Giorgia Meloni bate um recorde de longevidade política em Itália. José Carlos Duarte explica como moderou a imagem, segurou a coligação e se tornou uma figura central na Europa.

observador.title: 4h. Preço do petróleo sobe com a tensão no Médio Oriente
observador.description: Valores seguem a caminho do maior aumento semanal desde meados de julho, com o barrtil de Brent a registar uma subida de cerca de 15 cêntimos. Ainda, arranca esta sexta-feira A Festa do Avante!

observador.title: 3h. Investigação revela financiamento ilegal no Reform UK
observador.description: Nigel Farage e membros do Partido britânico Reform UK terão conspirardo para infringir a lei sobre doações estrangeiras a partidos. Ainda, Ministério da Justiça contradiz MAI sobre bidões com químicos

observador.title: 2h. Ministro do petróleo do irão garante manter exportações
observador.description: O ministro afirmou que a indústria petrolífera do país continua a contornar o bloqueio imposto pelas forças dos EUA. Ainda, JD Vance responsabiliza Irão e Europa pela subida de preço dos combustíveis

observador.title: 1h.Donald Trump anuncia novo secretário interino do Exército
observador.description: Adam Telle, atual secretário adjunto do Exército para Obras Civis, vai substituir Dan Driscoll, que apresentou a demissão na segunda-feira. Ainda, IL confirma que vai votar contra a moção de censura.

observador.title: A esquerda "sentadita" à vista da realidade
observador.description: É o teste mais simples e mais devastador das utopias políticas. Quando os seus corifeus recusam para si o risco que distribuem generosamente pela plebe, a hipocrisia fica exposta.

observador.title: Salvador, esta é a tua casa
observador.description: A vida tem muitas nuances, mas é difícil imaginar uma circunstância em que seja errado dizer a alguém: independentemente do que tens ou do que és, esta é a tua casa.

observador.title: A sociedade que odeia crianças
observador.description: Uma mulher que abranda a carreira por um filho "abdicou de si própria". Uma que abdica do filho pela carreira "escolheu a liberdade".

observador.title: 00h. Justiça contradiz Neves sobre custo de destruir bidões
observador.description: Ministério da Justiça não sabe quantos bidões ou processos estavam incluídos no valor. Ainda, há ainda cinco processos na Justiça que envolvem o ministro da Administração Interna.

observador.title: Do multiculturalismo à integração
observador.description: O multiculturalismo esquerdista não é islâmico. Serve-se do islamismo - em si, note-se, uma religião admirável - não para construir convivência e espiritualidade mas para atacar a cultura europeia.

observador.title: A Ascenção do Mal
observador.description: "The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing."

observador.title: PRR. Plano inicial com grandes obras foi "muito otimista"
observador.description: Fernando Alfaiate foi o "senhor PRR" nos últimos cinco anos. O prazo para a execução terminou a 31 de agosto, mas até ao fim do ano ainda há obras para fazer. Dinheiro não está garantido para todas.

observador.title: Luís Neves, o ministro “Al Capone” da República insolvente
observador.description: Luís Neves não foi ainda condenado por crime algum. Porém, já é o ministro “Al Capone” de uma República em insolvência. Al Capone tinha o Estado à perna. Luís Neves é obscenamente protegido por ele.

observador.title: Coimbra. SRAM prevê criar 530 novos empregos
observador.description: Com 57 milhões de investimento e apoio estatal de 30%, a multinacional norte-americana quer produzir em Portugal todos os componentes necessários para equipar uma bicicleta de raiz.

observador.title: Mais crianças do que mulheres em casas-abrigo
observador.description: É a primeira vez que o número de crianças é a maior fatia de vítimas acolhidas por situações de violência doméstica.

observador.title: Motoristas processam Uber por algoritmo salarial
observador.description: Ação coletiva reúne milhares de condutores de sete países da UE e Reino Unido. Peritos estimam perdas de até 7.500 euros por ano por motorista nos Países Baixos.

observador.description: No âmbito da redução de custos e corte do pessoal, que passa por mais de 100.000 despedimentos, uma publicação alemã teve acesso a um plano confidencial que revela o objectivo de encerrar a Seat.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

phys-org.title: Light-triggered interface lets adhesive peel cleanly and rebond through 15 cycles
phys-org.description: Adhesives are essential in electronics, vehicles and other products, but they can hinder repair and recycling when bonded parts are difficult to separate cleanly. A research team led by The University of Osaka has developed a prototype light-responsive adhesive that can be selectively detached from an illuminated surface without leaving observable residue. The adhesive film can then be rebonded by heating and reused after a second ultraviolet wavelength helps reset its molecular interactions.

phys-org.title: Tiny fossils reveal big insights about ant ancestors
phys-org.description: Two tiny ant fossils recovered in southern Saskatchewan are helping scientists better understand the evolutionary history of modern ants. Ant fossils dating from 72–56 million years ago are rare. What happened to insects such as ants during this period that saw a mass extinction wipe out all non-bird dinosaurs? How did that event reshape their world?

phys-org.title: From peas to potatoes, AI identifies nearly 800 promising plant proteins for food and cosmetics
phys-org.description: Scientists from Leeds' School of Food Science and Nutrition have developed an advanced AI process that can rapidly identify plant proteins capable of acting as emulsifiers from tens of millions of initial candidates. To date, it has identified nearly 800. The discovery will cut years of costly trial-and-error research and bring the next generation of plant-based foods and cosmetics closer.

phys-org.title: How an unassuming wildflower thrives in salt-laden air that kills other plants
phys-org.description: On the windswept coasts of Oregon and California lives an unassuming little plant that can withstand salty blasts that kill its inland counterparts. It's called the yellow monkeyflower. Now, researchers are beginning to understand how it manages to thrive in conditions that leave other plants burned, brown and withered.

phys-org.title: Warming seas could shrink most mollusks by 2100, but some may grow
phys-org.description: Research led by scientists at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette challenges a long-held assumption about the effects of climate change on marine life: Warmer oceans won't simply make animals smaller.

phys-org.title: Parliamentary motions show growing AI use, with no disclosure from MPs
phys-org.description: The two research teams have developed and used AI detectors trained on thousands of political motions in Sweden and the UK. What surprised the researchers was not that politicians were using AI—but that not a single one disclosed this openly.

phys-org.title: Iron helped scientists trace Earth's oxygen. Now it's telling a bigger story
phys-org.description: For decades, scientists have studied iron preserved in ancient rocks to reconstruct how Earth's oceans and atmosphere became rich in oxygen. A new study suggests iron has recorded other major transformations too.

phys-org.title: Built to last or break down: Ring size tunes biodegradable plastic lifetimes
phys-org.description: Biodegradable plastics should be tough enough for use yet able to break down at an appropriate rate afterward. Researchers at the University of Osaka show that changing the size of rings threaded onto a biodegradable polymer can tune both its toughness and enzymatic degradation, offering a way to design material lifetimes. The study is published in ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering.

phys-org.title: Satellites spot forest stress two years before bark beetle die-offs become apparent
phys-org.description: Satellite measurements detected declining photosynthetic activity in Western U.S. forests two years before bark beetle mortality appeared in aerial detection surveys, according to new University of Utah-led research.

phys-org.title: The Arctic melt season is a week longer now than it was in the 1980s, new research on sea ice trends shows
phys-org.description: Relatively few people have been to the Arctic, and even fewer have set foot in Antarctica. Most people rely on imagination and the media to visualize these landscapes and the ways they are changing.

phys-org.title: Microbes—dead or alive—can be early indicators of soil health under regenerative farming
phys-org.description: Researchers have demonstrated a series of biological tests that could serve as "proxies" for measuring how different regenerative agriculture practices could improve soil carbon—years before it would be possible to measure the carbon directly. The technique offers new insights into how effective various regenerative practices are at improving soil health.

phys-org.title: Even second graders can reason like scientists—if we ask them the right way
phys-org.description: When a child asks "Why does a blowfish puff up?" we often jump in with facts. But what if we paused and suggested that they ask instead, "How does a blowfish puff up?" It may seem like splitting hairs, but this small shift in phrasing could help reshape future generations' capacity for reasoning and critical thought in science and beyond.

phys-org.title: Nanoscale multiferroic materials open the path to efficient magnetic memory technology
phys-org.description: With the rapid spread of cloud computing, artificial intelligence and data centers, global energy consumption is rising to new heights. A promising way to reduce this burden is to develop memory devices that store information magnetically yet are written using electric fields. Magnetic memories are nonvolatile, meaning stored information is retained without a power supply.

phys-org.title: Predictive tools can confuse rare mutations with dangerous ones
phys-org.description: When a patient's DNA is read, it is compared with a reference version of the human genome. This allows geneticists and rare disease experts to look at a list of places where the patient's DNA differs. Most variations will be harmless and shared with millions of other people, but some can cause illness.

proj-syn.title: India’s Resilience Depends on Diversified Trade
proj-syn.description: India has signed a flurry of trade deals since Donald Trump’s return to the White House in an attempt to ensure that no single bilateral rupture will cause catastrophic harm. It should continue to expand its trade ties, while being wary of any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action vis-à-vis third countries.

proj-syn.title: Whipsaw Trade Policy Is Depressing Foreign Direct Investment
proj-syn.description: If a country opts for higher trade restrictions to promote its perceived domestic interests, a predictable policy is far superior to a volatile one. As new research shows, uncertainty causes unnecessary and large collateral damage to FDI inflows.

proj-syn.title: Why the Far Right’s War on Modern Architecture Matters
proj-syn.description: The Alternative for Germany’s fixation on architecture is more revealing than it may seem. Cultural policy is not only one area where the party can actually change conditions on the ground at the state level; it is also intimately tied to far-right forces’ exclusionary political agenda.

proj-syn.title: How Will the US-Iran War End?
proj-syn.description: The latest US effort to subdue Iran—an "economic D-Day" intended to cut off the Islamic Republic from the world economy—can’t succeed without the support of the country’s biggest trade partner. The only stable solution to the impasse in the Gulf is one that involves China and increases economic integration in the region.

proj-syn.title: Germany’s Political Firewall Is Crumbling
proj-syn.description: The upcoming election in Saxony-Anhalt could give the far-right Alternative für Deutschland control of a state government for the first time in Germany’s postwar history. Its rise offers a crucial lesson for democracies elsewhere: closing ranks against extremist parties is no substitute for effective governance.

proj-syn.title: The Swimmable City Test
proj-syn.description: In committing to provide a safe swimmable place within 15 minutes of every home by 2035, London Mayor Sadiq Khan has set a measurable, time-bound goal that cannot be met through a single program or line item on the budget. Instead, it requires a public mission capable of mobilizing all ministries and shaping markets.

proj-syn.title: The Tale of Economics
proj-syn.description: A new book tells the story of the economics discipline and its original purpose with a degree of verve and imaginativeness that puts dreary mainstream economists to shame. In the process, it gets at fundamental truths that major schools within the discipline have managed to obscure.

proj-syn.title: AI’s Market Path Will Get Bumpier
proj-syn.description: By enhancing the input that goes into so much of what we do—intelligence—AI’s potential to drive higher economic growth is enormous. But with fears of the technology's unintended consequences affecting the pace and depth of adoption, the promise of long-term gains must be set against more immediate risks.

proj-syn.title: American Götterdämmerung
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump and his Treasury secretary’s latest desperate threats confirm how much American power has waned on their watch. Far from compelling others to join their efforts to isolate Iran, they are hastening the transition to a post-American world order.

proj-syn.title: Hard Lessons for Europe From the Ceuta Crisis
proj-syn.description: European Union leaders should have received several messages during the recent surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In particular, cohesion without trust is fragile; dependence without limits leads to vulnerability; and selective enforcement of international law risks eroding a pillar of Europe’s strategic identity.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Silent Majority for International Cooperation
proj-syn.description: The hollowing out of global institutions has resulted in a rapid loss of credibility for the international rule of law. But a majority of people worldwide still recognize the value of multilateralism, which countries can preserve in the absence of superpower consent by finding better ways to cooperate.

proj-syn.title: Building Canada’s Post-American Economy
proj-syn.description: Canada’s dependence on the US market has become a strategic liability, leaving it vulnerable to President Donald Trump’s bullying. Reducing that dependence will require building industries that can compete globally while removing the structural barriers that prevent innovative Canadian firms from scaling.

proj-syn.title: Trump and Xi Should Align on AI
proj-syn.description: When potential outcomes are systemic and irreversible, preparation must precede certainty. This is the logic behind insurance, as well as every pandemic plan and arms-control treaty ever created, and it must be the principle that guides our approach to AI—beginning at the upcoming US-China summit.

proj-syn.title: The Quiet Revolution in Services
proj-syn.description: While economists debate whether industrialization can still play its traditional growth-promoting role in the current global and technological context, services have unexpectedly become an engine for economic development around the world. For developing and developed economies alike, the timing could not be better.

proj-syn.title: AI Addicts Won’t Make Better Workers
proj-syn.description: Economists widely agree that AI will boost labor productivity. But this view does not account for the possibility that hyperscalers will go all out to get people hooked on LLMs, because the narrower applications for which these tools are actually useful do not justify the massive investments made so far.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Crime Tax
proj-syn.description: Even excluding lives lost, communities displaced, and families ravaged, the economic costs of organized crime in the region produce a bleak picture, shaving 0.5–2 percentage points off annual GDP growth in the most affected countries. That, too, represents a hefty human toll.

proj-syn.title: Are The Walls Closing in on Bessent?
proj-syn.description: Far from suggesting financial Armageddon, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s futile efforts to keep a lid on Treasury yields suggest that, once again, the dollar is America’s currency, but everyone else’s problem. But while investors have few alternatives, the bond-salesman-in-chief cannot be complacent.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Reviving Chinese Marxist Economics
proj-syn.description: As recently as two years ago, most Chinese economists paid only lip service to Marxism and assigned Western textbooks to their students. The advent of AI has changed that, because the technology—open source and available to the smallest manufacturer for a pittance—promises to avoid the “rent trap” common to capitalist economies.
